canonical_definitions.description: The benchmark is present in reviewed public reporting for this release and the immediately preceding comparable reviewed release also reported it.
examples: Consecutive comparable releases both name the benchmark in reviewed reporting.
canonical_definitions.label: Continued

cautions: Dormant is not a claim about private evaluation or benchmark quality.
canonical_definitions.description: The first consecutive comparable reviewed successor omission after a qualifying occurrence.
examples: One fully reviewed comparable successor omits the benchmark.
canonical_definitions.label: Dormant in public reporting

cautions: This does not establish the first internal use of the benchmark.
canonical_definitions.description: The benchmark is present in reviewed public reporting for this release and has no earlier qualifying occurrence in the same comparable lineage.
examples: A benchmark first appears in the reviewed evidence for a lineage release.
canonical_definitions.label: First reported

cautions: The system must not advance dormant or outdated while evidence is insufficient.
canonical_definitions.description: Source coverage, successor order, lineage identity, or comparability is not strong enough to derive an omission status.
examples: A release has incomplete source review, so omission counting pauses.
canonical_definitions.label: Insufficient evidence

cautions: Absence from reviewed public reporting is not evidence that an evaluation was not run.
canonical_definitions.description: A comparable successor with complete source review does not name a benchmark previously reported in that lineage.
examples: The next comparable reviewed release omits a previously reported benchmark.
canonical_definitions.label: Not reported in reviewed successor

cautions: Outdated describes a public-reporting sequence and does not mean objectively obsolete.
canonical_definitions.description: The second and each later consecutive comparable reviewed successor omission after a qualifying occurrence.
examples: Two consecutive fully reviewed comparable successors omit the benchmark.
canonical_definitions.label: Outdated in public reporting

cautions: Quarantine records the gap without predicting what missing evidence would show.
canonical_definitions.description: A candidate or evidence record is withheld from verified occurrences because a concrete evidence gap remains.
examples: Public material does not identify the model precisely enough for a verified occurrence.
canonical_definitions.label: Quarantined

cautions: Returning does not imply that evaluation use stopped during the omission.
canonical_definitions.description: The benchmark is present after at least one comparable reviewed successor omitted it from public reporting.
examples: A later comparable release reports a benchmark after an intervening reviewed omission.
canonical_definitions.label: Returning
